Where it began

Harry Brook was born in Keighley on 22 February 1999 and grew up in Burley in Wharfedale, in a family that played plenty of club cricket. He went to Ilkley Grammar School and, at 14, moved on to Sedbergh School in Cumbria, where the school's coach, the former professional Martin Speight, did a great deal to shape him.

Yorkshire did not wait long. He played his first first-class match for them at Headingley in 2016, against Pakistan A, when he was a schoolboy. Two years later he captained England at the Under-19 World Cup, made an unbeaten 102 against Bangladesh, and finished as his side's top run-scorer.

The player

His first Test came against South Africa in September 2022, and by the end of that year he was making hundreds. On the tour of Pakistan that winter he top-scored in both innings of a win in Rawalpindi, his first Test century among them. In New Zealand in February 2023 he made 186, and after nine Test innings his 809 runs were more than anyone had managed at that stage. In 2024, again in Pakistan, he made 317, England's first Test triple hundred for 34 years, and shared a stand of 454 with Joe Root, a new Test record for the fourth wicket.

By October 2026 he had played 41 Tests, making 3,610 runs at an average of 53.09, with ten hundreds and 20 fifties, and had held 66 catches. England had made him their one-day and T20 captain in April 2025, and vice-captain of the Test side for the 2025-26 Ashes.

What made him special

Speed, mostly. He scored quickly without seeming to hurry: when he and Root lifted England from 21 for 3 at the Basin Reserve, his 186 came at better than a run a ball. Nor did a tight finish put him off. In 2025 he made a hundred in the fourth innings against India while England were chasing 374.

The bowling is a quieter story. By October 2026 his medium pace had brought him one Test wicket, at 127 runs each, which suggests England were wise to keep him in the batting order.

Away from the middle

He was part of the side that won the T20 World Cup in 2022, was named the ICC's Player of the Month twice that winter, and in 2023 the players' union, the Professional Cricketers' Association, voted him their best. He was also named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year. In the white-ball game he became, in 2026, the first captain of any side to hit a hundred at a T20 World Cup, and on 22 October 2026, in a tri-series in Pakistan, he made 202, the first ODI double hundred by an England batsman.

And finally

In 2023 he signed up as an ambassador for Major League Baseball in Europe, and the league's logo sits near the end of his bat. Plenty of baseball players would be pleased to strike the ball as often, and as far, as he does with it.
